headline: France fell in six weeks, Britain was bombed from the air, and Roosevelt took a third term
texture: The Battle of France opened in May, German armies broke the Maginot Line at Sedan, and the British Expeditionary Force was lifted off the beaches at Dunkirk between May 26 and early June. Petain became prime minister and asked Germany for terms. Italy declared war on France and Britain in June. Coventry city centre was destroyed from the air on November 14, and the RAF began bombing German cities two days later.

Roosevelt won a third term on November 5, which no president had done. Draft registration for about sixteen million men began in October and the Selective Service lottery was drawn in Washington on the twenty-ninth. Nylon stockings had gone on sale across the country in May, and almost five million pairs were bought on the first day. Cave paintings seventeen thousand years old were found at Lascaux in September by a group of boys.

Chaplin's The Great Dictator was the year's second-biggest picture, a comedy about Hitler that opened while Britain was being bombed. Boom Town outsold it and Rebecca came third, then won Best Picture. Artie Shaw's Frenesi was the best-selling record, on a Billboard chart that had only just started being compiled. Radio carried Europe into American dining rooms live, which no newsreel could do.

world.fall_of_france.label: France falls
world.fall_of_france.value: German armies broke through at Sedan in May and Petain asked Germany for peace terms in June
world.fall_of_france.detail: Edouard Daladier had resigned as prime minister on March 21 and Paul Reynaud succeeded him. Petain was made vice-premier on May 18.

world.dunkirk.label: Dunkirk evacuation
world.dunkirk.value: The British Expeditionary Force was lifted off the French coast from May 26
world.dunkirk.detail: Operation Aerial followed, evacuating Allied troops from elsewhere in France.

world.italy_declares_war.value: Declared war on France and the United Kingdom in June

world.coventry.label: Coventry Blitz
world.coventry.value: The city centre was destroyed by German bombing, and the RAF began bombing German cities two days later

notes: Research pass July 2026. Still an early-tier year, since the broadcast tier does not begin until 1950. This is the first year with a real chart to cite: Billboard's Best Selling Retail Records chart began being compiled this year, which is where the music.charts window opens. The fall of France and Italy's entry carry months rather than days because the source lists them under a month heading without a day. Babel being shot on Stalin's orders is general knowledge; the source says only that he was executed. American opinion opposing entry is a characterisation, not a sourced figure.
